[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//! While error structs are good for constrained cases, they don't
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//! allow for reporting multiple possible kinds of errors at one
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//! time. Error enums solve that problem.
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! SNAFU will read your error enum definition and create a *context
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//! selector* type for each variant (called `InvalidIdSnafu` in this
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//! example). These context selectors are used with the [`ensure!`][]
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! macro to provide ergonomic error creation:
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!

[141](https://docs.rs#141)//! enum Error {
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!     #[snafu(display("ID may not be less than 10, but it was {id}"))]
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//!     InvalidId { id: u16 },
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//! }
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//! fn is_valid_id(id: u16) -> Result<(), Error> {
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!     ensure!(id >= 10, InvalidIdSnafu { id });
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//!     Ok(())
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//! }
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! ```
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//! If you add a `source` field to a variant, you can then wrap an
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! underlying error using the [`context`](ResultExt::context)
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//! extension method:
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//!
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//! ```rust
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//! use snafu::prelude::*;
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//!
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//! #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! enum Error {
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//!     #[snafu(display("Could not read file {path}"))]
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//!     ConfigFile {
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//!         source: std::io::Error,
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!         path: String,
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!     },
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//! }
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!

[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!     std::fs::read_to_string(path).context(ConfigFileSnafu { path })
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! }
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//! ```
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//! You can combine the power of the [`whatever!`][] macro with an
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//! enum error type. This is great if you started out with
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//! [`Whatever`][] and are moving to a custom error type:
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//!
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! ```rust
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! use snafu::prelude::*;
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//!
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//! #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! enum Error {
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!     #[snafu(display("ID may not be less than 10, but it was {id}"))]
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//!     InvalidId { id: u16 },
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//!     #[snafu(whatever, display("{message}"))]
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//!     Whatever {
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//!         message: String,
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//!         #[snafu(source(from(Box<dyn std::error::Error>, Some)))]
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//!         source: Option<Box<dyn std::error::Error>>,
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//!     },
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//! }
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//!
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! fn is_valid_id(id: u16) -> Result<(), Error> {
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//!     ensure!(id >= 10, InvalidIdSnafu { id });
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//!     whatever!("Just kidding... this function always fails!");
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//!     Ok(())
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//! }
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//! ```
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//!
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//! You may wish to make the type `Send` and/or `Sync`, allowing
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! your error type to be used in multithreaded programs, by changing
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//! `dyn std::error::Error` to `dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync`.
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//!
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//! ## Reporting
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//!
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//! Printing an error via [`Display`][]
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//! will only show the top-level error message without the underlying sources.
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//! For an extended error report,
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//! SNAFU offers a user-friendly error output mechanism.
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//! It prints the main error and all underlying errors in the chain,
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//! from the most recent to the oldest,
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//! plus the [backtrace](Backtrace) if applicable.
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//! This is done by using the [`macro@report`] procedural macro
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//! or the [`Report`] type directly.
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//!
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//! ```no_run
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//! use snafu::prelude::*;
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//!
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//! #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//! #[snafu(display("Could not load configuration file {path}"))]
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//! struct ConfigFileError {
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//!     source: std::io::Error,
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//!     path: String,
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//! }
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//!
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//! fn read_config_file(path: &str) -> Result<String, ConfigFileError> {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//!     std::fs::read_to_string(path).context(ConfigFileSnafu { path })
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//! }
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//!
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//! #[snafu::report]
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//! fn main() -> Result<(), ConfigFileError> {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//!     read_config_file("bad-config.ini")?;
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//!     Ok(())
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//! }
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//! ```
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//!
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//! This will print:
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//!
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//! ```none
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//! Error: Could not load configuration file bad-config.ini
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//!
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//! Caused by this error:
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//! 1: No such file or directory (os error 2)
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//! ```
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//!
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//! Which shows the underlying errors, unlike [`Display`]:
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//!
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//! ```none
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//! Error: Could not load configuration file bad-config.ini
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//! ```
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//!
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//! ... and is also more readable than the [`Debug`] output:
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//!
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//! ```none
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//! Error: ConfigFileError { source: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: "No such file or directory" }, path: "bad-config.ini" }
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//! ```
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//!
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//! [`Display`]: core::fmt::Display
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//! [`Debug`]: core::fmt::Debug
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//!
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//! ## Next steps
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//!
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//! Read the documentation for the [`Snafu`][] macro to see all of the
[264](https://docs.rs#264)//! capabilities, then read the [user's guide](guide) for deeper
[265](https://docs.rs#265)//! understanding.

[428](https://docs.rs#428)/// Ensure a condition is true. If it is not, return from the function
[429](https://docs.rs#429)/// with an error.
[430](https://docs.rs#430)///
[431](https://docs.rs#431)/// ## Examples
[432](https://docs.rs#432)///
[433](https://docs.rs#433)/// ```rust
[434](https://docs.rs#434)/// use snafu::prelude::*;
[435](https://docs.rs#435)///
[436](https://docs.rs#436)/// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[437](https://docs.rs#437)/// enum Error {
[438](https://docs.rs#438)///     InvalidUser { user_id: i32 },
[439](https://docs.rs#439)/// }
[440](https://docs.rs#440)///
[441](https://docs.rs#441)/// fn example(user_id: i32) -> Result<(), Error> {
[442](https://docs.rs#442)///     ensure!(user_id > 0, InvalidUserSnafu { user_id });
[443](https://docs.rs#443)///     // After this point, we know that `user_id` is positive.
[444](https://docs.rs#444)///     let user_id = user_id as u32;
[445](https://docs.rs#445)///     Ok(())
[446](https://docs.rs#446)/// }
[447](https://docs.rs#447)/// ```
[448](https://docs.rs#448)#[macro_export]
[449](https://docs.rs#449)macro_rules! ensure {
[450](https://docs.rs#450)    ($predicate:expr, $context_selector:expr $(,)?) => {
[451](https://docs.rs#451)        if !$predicate {
[452](https://docs.rs#452)            return $context_selector
[453](https://docs.rs#453)                .fail()
[454](https://docs.rs#454)                .map_err(::core::convert::Into::into);
[455](https://docs.rs#455)        }
[456](https://docs.rs#456)    };
[457](https://docs.rs#457)}
[458](https://docs.rs#458)
[459](https://docs.rs#459)#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[460](https://docs.rs#460)#[doc(hidden)]
[461](https://docs.rs#461)pub use alloc::format as __format;
[462](https://docs.rs#462)
[463](https://docs.rs#463)/// Instantiate and return a stringly-typed error message.
[464](https://docs.rs#464)///
[465](https://docs.rs#465)/// This can be used with the provided [`Whatever`][] type or with a
[466](https://docs.rs#466)/// custom error type that uses `snafu(whatever)`.
[467](https://docs.rs#467)///
[468](https://docs.rs#468)/// # Without an underlying error
[469](https://docs.rs#469)///
[470](https://docs.rs#470)/// Provide a format string and any optional arguments. The macro will
[471](https://docs.rs#471)/// unconditionally exit the calling function with an error.
[472](https://docs.rs#472)///
[473](https://docs.rs#473)/// ## Examples
[474](https://docs.rs#474)///
[475](https://docs.rs#475)/// ```rust
[476](https://docs.rs#476)/// use snafu::{Whatever, prelude::*};
[477](https://docs.rs#477)///
[478](https://docs.rs#478)/// type Result<T, E = Whatever> = std::result::Result<T, E>;
[479](https://docs.rs#479)///
[480](https://docs.rs#480)/// enum Status {
[481](https://docs.rs#481)///     Sleeping,
[482](https://docs.rs#482)///     Chilling,
[483](https://docs.rs#483)///     Working,
[484](https://docs.rs#484)/// }
[485](https://docs.rs#485)///
[486](https://docs.rs#486)/// # fn stand_up() {}
[487](https://docs.rs#487)/// # fn go_downstairs() {}
[488](https://docs.rs#488)/// fn do_laundry(status: Status, items: u8) -> Result<()> {
[489](https://docs.rs#489)///     match status {
[490](https://docs.rs#490)///         Status::Sleeping => whatever!("Cannot launder {items} clothes when I am asleep"),
[491](https://docs.rs#491)///         Status::Chilling => {
[492](https://docs.rs#492)///             stand_up();
[493](https://docs.rs#493)///             go_downstairs();
[494](https://docs.rs#494)///         }
[495](https://docs.rs#495)///         Status::Working => {
[496](https://docs.rs#496)///             go_downstairs();
[497](https://docs.rs#497)///         }
[498](https://docs.rs#498)///     }
[499](https://docs.rs#499)///     Ok(())
[500](https://docs.rs#500)/// }
[501](https://docs.rs#501)/// ```
[502](https://docs.rs#502)///
[503](https://docs.rs#503)/// # With an underlying error
[504](https://docs.rs#504)///
[505](https://docs.rs#505)/// Provide a `Result` as the first argument, followed by a format
[506](https://docs.rs#506)/// string and any optional arguments. If the `Result` is an error,
[507](https://docs.rs#507)/// the formatted string will be appended to the error and the macro
[508](https://docs.rs#508)/// will exit the calling function with an error. If the `Result` is
[509](https://docs.rs#509)/// not an error, the macro will evaluate to the `Ok` value of the
[510](https://docs.rs#510)/// `Result`.
[511](https://docs.rs#511)///
[512](https://docs.rs#512)/// ## Examples
[513](https://docs.rs#513)///
[514](https://docs.rs#514)/// ```rust
[515](https://docs.rs#515)/// use snafu::prelude::*;
[516](https://docs.rs#516)///
[517](https://docs.rs#517)/// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[518](https://docs.rs#518)/// #[snafu(whatever, display("Error was: {message}"))]
[519](https://docs.rs#519)/// struct Error {
[520](https://docs.rs#520)///     message: String,
[521](https://docs.rs#521)///     #[snafu(source(from(Box<dyn std::error::Error>, Some)))]
[522](https://docs.rs#522)///     source: Option<Box<dyn std::error::Error>>,
[523](https://docs.rs#523)/// }
[524](https://docs.rs#524)/// type Result<T, E = Error> = std::result::Result<T, E>;
[525](https://docs.rs#525)///
[526](https://docs.rs#526)/// fn calculate_brightness_factor() -> Result<u8> {
[527](https://docs.rs#527)///     let angle = calculate_angle_of_refraction();
[528](https://docs.rs#528)///     let angle = whatever!(angle, "There was no angle");
[529](https://docs.rs#529)///     Ok(angle * 2)
[530](https://docs.rs#530)/// }
[531](https://docs.rs#531)///
[532](https://docs.rs#532)/// fn calculate_angle_of_refraction() -> Result<u8> {
[533](https://docs.rs#533)///     whatever!("The programmer forgot to implement this...");
[534](https://docs.rs#534)/// }
[535](https://docs.rs#535)/// ```
[536](https://docs.rs#536)#[macro_export]
[537](https://docs.rs#537)#[cfg(any(feature = "alloc", test))]
[538](https://docs.rs#538)macro_rules! whatever {
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    ($fmt:literal$(, $($arg:expr),* $(,)?)?) => {
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        return core::result::Result::Err({
[541](https://docs.rs#541)            $crate::FromString::without_source(
[542](https://docs.rs#542)                $crate::__format!($fmt$(, $($arg),*)*),
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            )
[544](https://docs.rs#544)        });
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    };
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    ($source:expr, $fmt:literal$(, $($arg:expr),* $(,)?)*) => {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)        match $source {
[548](https://docs.rs#548)            core::result::Result::Ok(v) => v,
[549](https://docs.rs#549)            core::result::Result::Err(e) => {
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                return core::result::Result::Err({
[551](https://docs.rs#551)                    $crate::FromString::with_source(
[552](https://docs.rs#552)                        core::convert::Into::into(e),
[553](https://docs.rs#553)                        $crate::__format!($fmt$(, $($arg),*)*),
[554](https://docs.rs#554)                    )
[555](https://docs.rs#555)                });
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            }
[557](https://docs.rs#557)        }
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    };
[559](https://docs.rs#559)}
[560](https://docs.rs#560)
[561](https://docs.rs#561)/// Ensure a condition is true. If it is not, return a stringly-typed
[562](https://docs.rs#562)/// error message.
[563](https://docs.rs#563)///
[564](https://docs.rs#564)/// This can be used with the provided [`Whatever`][] type or with a
[565](https://docs.rs#565)/// custom error type that uses `snafu(whatever)`.
[566](https://docs.rs#566)///
[567](https://docs.rs#567)/// ## Examples
[568](https://docs.rs#568)///
[569](https://docs.rs#569)/// ```rust
[570](https://docs.rs#570)/// use snafu::prelude::*;
[571](https://docs.rs#571)///
[572](https://docs.rs#572)/// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[573](https://docs.rs#573)/// #[snafu(whatever, display("Error was: {message}"))]
[574](https://docs.rs#574)/// struct Error {
[575](https://docs.rs#575)///     message: String,
[576](https://docs.rs#576)/// }
[577](https://docs.rs#577)/// type Result<T, E = Error> = std::result::Result<T, E>;
[578](https://docs.rs#578)///
[579](https://docs.rs#579)/// fn get_bank_account_balance(account_id: &str) -> Result<u8> {
[580](https://docs.rs#580)/// # fn moon_is_rising() -> bool { false }
[581](https://docs.rs#581)///     ensure_whatever!(
[582](https://docs.rs#582)///         moon_is_rising(),
[583](https://docs.rs#583)///         "We are recalibrating the dynamos for account {account_id}, sorry",
[584](https://docs.rs#584)///     );
[585](https://docs.rs#585)///
[586](https://docs.rs#586)///     Ok(100)
[587](https://docs.rs#587)/// }
[588](https://docs.rs#588)/// ```
[589](https://docs.rs#589)#[macro_export]
[590](https://docs.rs#590)#[cfg(any(feature = "alloc", test))]
[591](https://docs.rs#591)macro_rules! ensure_whatever {
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    ($predicate:expr, $fmt:literal$(, $($arg:expr),* $(,)?)?) => {
[593](https://docs.rs#593)        if !$predicate {
[594](https://docs.rs#594)            $crate::whatever!($fmt$(, $($arg),*)*);
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        }
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    };
[597](https://docs.rs#597)}
[598](https://docs.rs#598)
[599](https://docs.rs#599)/// Additions to [`Result`][].
[600](https://docs.rs#600)pub trait ResultExt<T, E>: Sized {
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    /// Extend a [`Result`]'s error with additional context-sensitive information.
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    ///
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    /// [`Result`]: std::result::Result
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    ///
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    /// ```rust
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    /// use snafu::prelude::*;
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    ///
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    /// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    /// enum Error {
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    ///     Authenticating {
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    ///         user_name: String,
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    ///         user_id: i32,
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    ///         source: ApiError,
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    ///     },
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    /// }
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    ///
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    /// fn example() -> Result<(), Error> {
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    ///     another_function().context(AuthenticatingSnafu {
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    ///         user_name: "admin",
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    ///         user_id: 42,
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    ///     })?;
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    ///     Ok(())
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    /// }
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    ///
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// # type ApiError = Box<dyn std::error::Error>;
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    /// fn another_function() -> Result<i32, ApiError> {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    ///     /* ... */
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    /// # Ok(42)
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// }
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    /// ```
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    ///
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    /// Note that the context selector will call [`Into::into`][] on each field,
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    /// so the types are not required to exactly match.
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    fn context<C, E2>(self, context: C) -> Result<T, E2>
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    where
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        C: IntoError<E2, Source = E>,
[637](https://docs.rs#637)        E2: Error + ErrorCompat;
[638](https://docs.rs#638)
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    /// Extend a [`Result`][]'s error with lazily-generated context-sensitive information.
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    ///
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    /// [`Result`]: std::result::Result
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    ///
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    /// ```rust
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    /// use snafu::prelude::*;
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    ///
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    /// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[647](https://docs.rs#647)    /// enum Error {
[648](https://docs.rs#648)    ///     Authenticating {
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    ///         user_name: String,
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    ///         user_id: i32,
[651](https://docs.rs#651)    ///         source: ApiError,
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    ///     },
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    /// }
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    ///
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    /// fn example() -> Result<(), Error> {
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    ///     another_function().with_context(|_| AuthenticatingSnafu {
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    ///         user_name: "admin".to_string(),
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    ///         user_id: 42,
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    ///     })?;
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    ///     Ok(())
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    /// }
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    ///
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    /// # type ApiError = std::io::Error;
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    /// fn another_function() -> Result<i32, ApiError> {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    ///     /* ... */
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    /// # Ok(42)
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    /// }
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    /// ```
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    ///
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    /// Note that this *may not* be needed in many cases because the context
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    /// selector will call [`Into::into`][] on each field.
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    fn with_context<F, C, E2>(self, context: F) -> Result<T, E2>
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    where
[674](https://docs.rs#674)        F: FnOnce(&mut E) -> C,
[675](https://docs.rs#675)        C: IntoError<E2, Source = E>,
[676](https://docs.rs#676)        E2: Error + ErrorCompat;
[677](https://docs.rs#677)
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    /// Extend a [`Result`]'s error with information from a string.
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    ///
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    /// The target error type must implement [`FromString`] by using
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    /// the
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    /// [`#[snafu(whatever)]`][Snafu#controlling-stringly-typed-errors]
[683](https://docs.rs#683)    /// attribute. The premade [`Whatever`] type is also available.
[684](https://docs.rs#684)    ///
[685](https://docs.rs#685)    /// In many cases, you will want to use
[686](https://docs.rs#686)    /// [`with_whatever_context`][Self::with_whatever_context] instead
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    /// as it gives you access to the error and is only called in case
[688](https://docs.rs#688)    /// of error. This method is best suited for when you have a
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    /// string literal.
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    ///
[691](https://docs.rs#691)    /// ```rust
[692](https://docs.rs#692)    /// use snafu::{prelude::*, Whatever};
[693](https://docs.rs#693)    ///
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    /// fn example() -> Result<(), Whatever> {
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    ///     std::fs::read_to_string("/this/does/not/exist")
[696](https://docs.rs#696)    ///         .whatever_context("couldn't open the file")?;
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    ///     Ok(())
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    /// }
[699](https://docs.rs#699)    ///
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    /// let err = example().unwrap_err();
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    /// assert_eq!("couldn't open the file", err.to_string());
[702](https://docs.rs#702)    /// ```
[703](https://docs.rs#703)    #[cfg(any(feature = "alloc", test))]
[704](https://docs.rs#704)    fn whatever_context<S, E2>(self, context: S) -> Result<T, E2>
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    where
[706](https://docs.rs#706)        S: Into<String>,
[707](https://docs.rs#707)        E2: FromString,
[708](https://docs.rs#708)        E: Into<E2::Source>;
[709](https://docs.rs#709)
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    /// Extend a [`Result`]'s error with information from a
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// lazily-generated string.
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    ///
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    /// The target error type must implement [`FromString`] by using
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    /// the
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    /// [`#[snafu(whatever)]`][Snafu#controlling-stringly-typed-errors]
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// attribute. The premade [`Whatever`] type is also available.
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    ///
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    /// ```rust
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    /// use snafu::{prelude::*, Whatever};
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    ///
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    /// fn example() -> Result<(), Whatever> {
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    ///     let filename = "/this/does/not/exist";
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    ///     std::fs::read_to_string(filename)
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    ///         .with_whatever_context(|_| format!("couldn't open the file {filename}"))?;
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    ///     Ok(())
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    /// }
[727](https://docs.rs#727)    ///
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    /// let err = example().unwrap_err();
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    /// assert_eq!(
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    ///     "couldn't open the file /this/does/not/exist",
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    ///     err.to_string(),
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    /// );
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    /// ```
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    ///
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    /// The closure is not called when the `Result` is `Ok`:
[736](https://docs.rs#736)    ///
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    /// ```rust
[738](https://docs.rs#738)    /// use snafu::{prelude::*, Whatever};
[739](https://docs.rs#739)    ///
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    /// let value: std::io::Result<i32> = Ok(42);
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    /// let result = value.with_whatever_context::<_, String, Whatever>(|_| {
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    ///     panic!("This block will not be evaluated");
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    /// });
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    ///
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    /// assert!(result.is_ok());
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    /// ```
[747](https://docs.rs#747)    #[cfg(any(feature = "alloc", test))]
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    fn with_whatever_context<F, S, E2>(self, context: F) -> Result<T, E2>
[749](https://docs.rs#749)    where
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        F: FnOnce(&mut E) -> S,
[751](https://docs.rs#751)        S: Into<String>,
[752](https://docs.rs#752)        E2: FromString,
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        E: Into<E2::Source>;
[754](https://docs.rs#754)
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    /// Convert a [`Result`]'s error into a boxed trait object
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    /// compatible with multiple threads.
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    ///
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    /// This is useful when you have errors of multiple types that you
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    /// wish to treat as one type. This may occur when dealing with
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    /// errors in a generic context, such as when the error is a
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    /// trait's associated type.
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    ///
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    /// In cases like this, you cannot name the original error type
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    /// without making the outer error type generic as well. Using an
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    /// error trait object offers an alternate solution.
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    ///
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    /// ```rust
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    /// # use std::convert::TryInto;
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    /// use snafu::prelude::*;
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    ///
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    /// fn convert_value_into_u8<V>(v: V) -> Result<u8, ConversionFailedError>
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    /// where
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    ///     V: TryInto<u8>,
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    ///     V::Error: snafu::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    /// {
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    ///     v.try_into().boxed().context(ConversionFailedSnafu)
[777](https://docs.rs#777)    /// }
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    ///
[779](https://docs.rs#779)    /// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    /// struct ConversionFailedError {
[781](https://docs.rs#781)    ///     source: Box<dyn snafu::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>,
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    /// }
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    /// ```
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    ///
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    /// ## Avoiding misapplication
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    ///
[787](https://docs.rs#787)    /// We recommended **against** using this to create fewer error
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    /// variants which in turn would group unrelated errors. While
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    /// convenient for the programmer, doing so usually makes lower
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    /// quality error messages for the user.
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    ///
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    /// ```rust
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    /// use snafu::prelude::*;
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    /// use std::fs;
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    ///
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    /// fn do_not_do_this() -> Result<i32, UselessError> {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    ///     let content = fs::read_to_string("/path/to/config/file")
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    ///         .boxed()
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    ///         .context(UselessSnafu)?;
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    ///     content.parse().boxed().context(UselessSnafu)
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    /// }
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    ///
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    /// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[804](https://docs.rs#804)    /// struct UselessError {
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    ///     source: Box<dyn snafu::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>,
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    /// }
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    /// ```
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    #[cfg(any(feature = "alloc", test))]
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    fn boxed<'a>(self) -> Result<T, Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync + 'a>>
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    where
[811](https://docs.rs#811)        E: Error + Send + Sync + 'a;
[812](https://docs.rs#812)
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    /// Convert a [`Result`]'s error into a boxed trait object.
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    ///
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    /// This is useful when you have errors of multiple types that you
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    /// wish to treat as one type. This may occur when dealing with
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    /// errors in a generic context, such as when the error is a
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    /// trait's associated type.
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    ///
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    /// In cases like this, you cannot name the original error type
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    /// without making the outer error type generic as well. Using an
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    /// error trait object offers an alternate solution.
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    ///
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    /// ```rust
[825](https://docs.rs#825)    /// # use std::convert::TryInto;
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    /// use snafu::prelude::*;
[827](https://docs.rs#827)    ///
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    /// fn convert_value_into_u8<V>(v: V) -> Result<u8, ConversionFailedError>
[829](https://docs.rs#829)    /// where
[830](https://docs.rs#830)    ///     V: TryInto<u8>,
[831](https://docs.rs#831)    ///     V::Error: snafu::Error + 'static,
[832](https://docs.rs#832)    /// {
[833](https://docs.rs#833)    ///     v.try_into().boxed_local().context(ConversionFailedSnafu)
[834](https://docs.rs#834)    /// }
[835](https://docs.rs#835)    ///
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    /// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    /// struct ConversionFailedError {
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    ///     source: Box<dyn snafu::Error + 'static>,
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    /// }
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    /// ```
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    ///
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    /// ## Avoiding misapplication
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    ///
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    /// We recommended **against** using this to create fewer error
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    /// variants which in turn would group unrelated errors. While
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    /// convenient for the programmer, doing so usually makes lower
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    /// quality error messages for the user.
[848](https://docs.rs#848)    ///
[849](https://docs.rs#849)    /// ```rust
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    /// use snafu::prelude::*;
[851](https://docs.rs#851)    /// use std::fs;
[852](https://docs.rs#852)    ///
[853](https://docs.rs#853)    /// fn do_not_do_this() -> Result<i32, UselessError> {
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    ///     let content = fs::read_to_string("/path/to/config/file")
[855](https://docs.rs#855)    ///         .boxed_local()
[856](https://docs.rs#856)    ///         .context(UselessSnafu)?;
[857](https://docs.rs#857)    ///     content.parse().boxed_local().context(UselessSnafu)
[858](https://docs.rs#858)    /// }
[859](https://docs.rs#859)    ///
[860](https://docs.rs#860)    /// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[861](https://docs.rs#861)    /// struct UselessError {
[862](https://docs.rs#862)    ///     source: Box<dyn snafu::Error + 'static>,
[863](https://docs.rs#863)    /// }
[864](https://docs.rs#864)    /// ```
[865](https://docs.rs#865)    #[cfg(any(feature = "alloc", test))]
[866](https://docs.rs#866)    fn boxed_local<'a>(self) -> Result<T, Box<dyn Error + 'a>>
[867](https://docs.rs#867)    where
[868](https://docs.rs#868)        E: Error + 'a;
[869](https://docs.rs#869)}
[870](https://docs.rs#870)
[871](https://docs.rs#871)impl<T, E> ResultExt<T, E> for Result<T, E> {
[872](https://docs.rs#872)    #[track_caller]
[873](https://docs.rs#873)    fn context<C, E2>(self, context: C) -> Result<T, E2>
[874](https://docs.rs#874)    where
[875](https://docs.rs#875)        C: IntoError<E2, Source = E>,
[876](https://docs.rs#876)        E2: Error + ErrorCompat,
[877](https://docs.rs#877)    {
[878](https://docs.rs#878)        // https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/74042
[879](https://docs.rs#879)        match self {
[880](https://docs.rs#880)            Ok(v) => Ok(v),
[881](https://docs.rs#881)            Err(error) => Err(context.into_error(error)),
[882](https://docs.rs#882)        }
[883](https://docs.rs#883)    }
[884](https://docs.rs#884)
[885](https://docs.rs#885)    #[track_caller]
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    fn with_context<F, C, E2>(self, context: F) -> Result<T, E2>
[887](https://docs.rs#887)    where
[888](https://docs.rs#888)        F: FnOnce(&mut E) -> C,
[889](https://docs.rs#889)        C: IntoError<E2, Source = E>,
[890](https://docs.rs#890)        E2: Error + ErrorCompat,
[891](https://docs.rs#891)    {
[892](https://docs.rs#892)        // https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/74042
[893](https://docs.rs#893)        match self {
[894](https://docs.rs#894)            Ok(v) => Ok(v),
[895](https://docs.rs#895)            Err(mut error) => {
[896](https://docs.rs#896)                let context = context(&mut error);
[897](https://docs.rs#897)                Err(context.into_error(error))
[898](https://docs.rs#898)            }
[899](https://docs.rs#899)        }
[900](https://docs.rs#900)    }
[901](https://docs.rs#901)
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    #[cfg(any(feature = "alloc", test))]
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    #[track_caller]
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    fn whatever_context<S, E2>(self, context: S) -> Result<T, E2>
[905](https://docs.rs#905)    where
[906](https://docs.rs#906)        S: Into<String>,
[907](https://docs.rs#907)        E2: FromString,
[908](https://docs.rs#908)        E: Into<E2::Source>,
[909](https://docs.rs#909)    {
[910](https://docs.rs#910)        // https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/74042
[911](https://docs.rs#911)        match self {
[912](https://docs.rs#912)            Ok(v) => Ok(v),
[913](https://docs.rs#913)            Err(error) => Err(FromString::with_source(error.into(), context.into())),
[914](https://docs.rs#914)        }
[915](https://docs.rs#915)    }
[916](https://docs.rs#916)
[917](https://docs.rs#917)    #[cfg(any(feature = "alloc", test))]
[918](https://docs.rs#918)    #[track_caller]
[919](https://docs.rs#919)    fn with_whatever_context<F, S, E2>(self, context: F) -> Result<T, E2>
[920](https://docs.rs#920)    where
[921](https://docs.rs#921)        F: FnOnce(&mut E) -> S,
[922](https://docs.rs#922)        S: Into<String>,
[923](https://docs.rs#923)        E2: FromString,
[924](https://docs.rs#924)        E: Into<E2::Source>,
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    {
[926](https://docs.rs#926)        // https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/74042
[927](https://docs.rs#927)        match self {
[928](https://docs.rs#928)            Ok(t) => Ok(t),
[929](https://docs.rs#929)            Err(mut e) => {

[931](https://docs.rs#931)                Err(FromString::with_source(e.into(), context.into()))
[932](https://docs.rs#932)            }
[933](https://docs.rs#933)        }
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    }

[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)    /// Convert an [`Option`] into a [`Result`] with information

[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)    /// });
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)    ///

[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)    /// ```

[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)/// Backports changes to the [`Error`][] trait to versions of Rust
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)/// lacking them.
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)///
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)/// It is recommended to always call these methods explicitly so that
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)/// it is easy to replace usages of this trait when you start
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)/// supporting a newer version of Rust.
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)///
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)/// ```
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)/// # use snafu::{prelude::*, ErrorCompat};
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)/// # #[derive(Debug, Snafu)] enum Example {};
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)/// # fn example(error: Example) {
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)/// ErrorCompat::backtrace(&error); // Recommended
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)/// error.backtrace();              // Discouraged
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)/// # }
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)/// ```
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)pub trait ErrorCompat {
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)    /// Returns a [`Backtrace`][] that may be printed.
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)    fn backtrace(&self) -> Option<&Backtrace> {
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)        None
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)    }
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)    /// Returns an iterator for traversing the chain of errors,
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)    /// starting with the current error
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)    /// and continuing with recursive calls to `Error::source`.
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)    ///
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)    /// To omit the current error and only traverse its sources,
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)    /// use `skip(1)`.
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)    fn iter_chain(&self) -> ChainCompat<'_, '_>
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)    where
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)        Self: AsErrorSource,
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)    {
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)        ChainCompat::new(self.as_error_source())
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)    }

[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)/// Converts the receiver into an [`Error`][] trait object, suitable
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)/// for use in [`Error::source`][].
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)///
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)/// It is expected that most users of SNAFU will not directly interact
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)/// with this trait.
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)///
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)/// [`Error`]: std::error::Error
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)/// [`Error::source`]: std::error::Error::source
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)//
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)// Given an error enum with multiple types of underlying causes:
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)//
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)// ```rust
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)// enum Error {
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)//     BoxTraitObjectSendSync(Box<dyn error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>),
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)//     BoxTraitObject(Box<dyn error::Error + 'static>),
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)//     Boxed(Box<io::Error>),
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)//     Unboxed(io::Error),
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)// }
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)// ```
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)//
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)// This trait provides the answer to what consistent expression can go
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)// in each match arm:
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)//
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)// ```rust
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)// impl error::Error for Error {
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)//     fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn error::Error + 'static)> {
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)//         use Error::*;
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)//
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)//         let v = match *self {
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)//             BoxTraitObjectSendSync(ref e) => ...,
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)//             BoxTraitObject(ref e) => ...,
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)//             Boxed(ref e) => ...,
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)//             Unboxed(ref e) => ...,
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)//         };
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)//
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)//         Some(v)
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)//     }
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)// }
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)//
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)// Existing methods like returning `e`, `&**e`, `Borrow::borrow(e)`,
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)// `Deref::deref(e)`, and `AsRef::as_ref(e)` do not work for various
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)// reasons.
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)pub trait AsErrorSource {
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)    /// For maximum effectiveness, this needs to be called as a method
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)    /// to benefit from Rust's automatic dereferencing of method
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)    /// receivers.
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)    fn as_error_source(&self) -> &(dyn Error + 'static);
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)}
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)impl AsErrorSource for dyn Error + 'static {
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)    fn as_error_source(&self) -> &(dyn Error + 'static) {
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)        self
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)    }
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)}
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)impl AsErrorSource for dyn Error + Send + 'static {
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)    fn as_error_source(&self) -> &(dyn Error + 'static) {
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)        self
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    }
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)}
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)impl AsErrorSource for dyn Error + Sync + 'static {
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)    fn as_error_source(&self) -> &(dyn Error + 'static) {
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)        self
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)    }
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)}

[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)/// Only create a backtrace when an environment variable is set.
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)///
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)/// This looks first for the value of `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE` then
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)/// `RUST_BACKTRACE`. If the value is set to `1`, backtraces will be
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)/// enabled.
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)///
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)/// This value will be tested only once per program execution;
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)/// changing the environment variable after it has been checked will
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)/// have no effect.
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)///
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)/// ## Interaction with the Provider API
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)///
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)/// If you enable the [`unstable-provider-api` feature
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)/// flag][provider-ff], a backtrace will not be captured if the
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)/// original error is able to provide a `Backtrace`, even if the
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)/// appropriate environment variables are set. This prevents capturing
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)/// a redundant backtrace.
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)///
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)/// [provider-ff]: crate::guide::feature_flags#unstable-provider-api
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)#[cfg(any(feature = "std", test))]
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)impl GenerateImplicitData for Option<Backtrace> {
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)    fn generate() -> Self {
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)        if backtrace_collection_enabled() {
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)            Some(Backtrace::generate())
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)        } else {
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)            None
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)        }
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)    }
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)    fn generate_with_source(source: &dyn crate::Error) -> Self {
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)        #[cfg(feature = "unstable-provider-api")]
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)        {
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)            if !backtrace_collection_enabled() {
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)                None
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)            } else if backtraces(source).next().is_some() {
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)                None
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)            } else {
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)                Some(Backtrace::generate_with_source(source))
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)            }
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)        }
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)        #[cfg(not(feature = "unstable-provider-api"))]
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)        {
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)            let _source = source;
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)            Self::generate()
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)        }
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    }
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)}

[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)#[cfg(any(feature = "std", test))]
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)fn backtrace_collection_enabled() -> bool {
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)    use crate::once_bool::OnceBool;
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    use std::env;
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    static ENABLED: OnceBool = OnceBool::new();
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)    ENABLED.get(|| {
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)        // TODO: What values count as "true"?
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)        env::var_os("RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE")
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)            .or_else(|| env::var_os("RUST_BACKTRACE"))
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)            .map_or(false, |v| v == "1")
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)    })

[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)/// The source code location where the error was reported.
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)///
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)/// To use it, add a field of type `Location` to your error and
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)/// register it as [implicitly generated data][implicit]. When
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)/// constructing the error, you do not need to provide the location:
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)///
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)/// ```rust
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)/// # use snafu::prelude::*;
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)/// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)/// struct NeighborhoodError {
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)///     #[snafu(implicit)]
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)///     loc: snafu::Location,
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)/// }
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)///
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)/// fn check_next_door() -> Result<(), NeighborhoodError> {
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)///     ensure!(everything_quiet(), NeighborhoodSnafu);
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)///     Ok(())
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)/// }
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)/// # fn everything_quiet() -> bool { false }
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)/// ```
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)///
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)/// [implicit]: Snafu#controlling-implicitly-generated-data
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)///
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)/// ## Limitations
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)///
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)/// Implicitly generated data, including `Location`, is generated when
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)/// the wrapping error value is constructed:
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)///
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)/// ```rust
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)/// # use snafu::{prelude::*, Location, location};
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)/// # fn fallible_code() -> Result<(), InnerError> { Err(InnerError) }
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)/// # #[derive(Debug, Snafu)] struct InnerError;
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)/// # #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)/// # struct InterestingError {
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)/// #   source: InnerError,
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)/// #   #[snafu(implicit)] location: Location,
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)/// # }
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)/// # let base_loc = location!();
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)/// # let r: Result<(), InterestingError> = (|| {
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)/// // The first we know about the error is on this line:
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)/// let e = fallible_code();
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)/// // but the location will correspond to this line:
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)/// e.context(InterestingSnafu)?;
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)/// # Ok(())
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)/// # })();
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)/// # let e = r.unwrap_err();
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)/// # assert_eq!(e.location.line(), base_loc.line() + 5);
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)/// ```
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)///
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)/// If you have [disabled the context selector][disabled], the
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)/// `Location` will correspond to where the `From` implementation is
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)/// invoked. This is usually part of the `?` operator:
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)///
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)/// ```rust
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)/// # use snafu::{prelude::*, Location, location};
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)/// # fn fallible_code() -> Result<(), InnerError> { Err(InnerError) }
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)/// # #[derive(Debug, Snafu)] struct InnerError;
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)/// # #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)/// # #[snafu(context(false))]
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)/// # struct InterestingError {
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)/// #   source: InnerError,
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)/// #   #[snafu(implicit)] location: Location,
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)/// # }
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)/// # let base_loc = location!();
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)/// # let r: Result<(), InterestingError> = (|| {
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)/// // The first we know about the error is on this line:
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)/// let e = fallible_code();
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)/// // but the location will correspond to this line:
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)/// e?;
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)/// # Ok(())
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)/// # })();
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)/// # let e = r.unwrap_err();
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)/// # assert_eq!(e.location.line(), base_loc.line() + 5);
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)/// ```
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)///
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)/// Inspecting the code at the generated `Location` will usually
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)/// quickly lead back to the original error, but it's recommended to
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)/// create the wrapping error as close to the original error location
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)/// to reduce confusion.
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)///
[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)/// [disabled]: Snafu#disabling-the-context-selector
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)///
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)/// ### Asynchronous code
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)///
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)/// When using SNAFU's
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)#[cfg_attr(feature = "futures", doc = " [`TryFutureExt`][futures::TryFutureExt]")]
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "futures"), doc = " `TryFutureExt`")]
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)/// or
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)#[cfg_attr(feature = "futures", doc = " [`TryStreamExt`][futures::TryStreamExt]")]
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "futures"), doc = " `TryStreamExt`")]
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)/// extension traits, the automatically captured location will
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)/// correspond to where the future or stream was **polled**, not where
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)/// it was created. Additionally, many `Future` or `Stream`
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)/// combinators do not forward the caller's location to their
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)/// closures, causing the recorded location to be inside of the future
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)/// combinator's library.
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)///
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)/// There are two workarounds:
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)/// 1. Avoid combinators and use the non-async [`ResultExt`]
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)/// 1. Construct the location explicitly, such as by the [`location!`] macro
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)///
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)/// ```rust
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)/// # #[cfg(all(feature = "futures", feature = "internal-dev-dependencies"))] {
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)/// # use snafu::{prelude::*, Location, location};
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)/// # let body = async {
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)/// // Non-ideal: will report where `wrapped_error_future` is `.await`ed.
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)/// # let base_location = location!();
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)/// # let error_future = async { AnotherSnafu.fail::<()>() };
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)/// let wrapped_error_future = error_future.context(ImplicitLocationSnafu);
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)/// # let wrapped_error = wrapped_error_future.await.unwrap_err();
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)/// # assert_eq!(wrapped_error.location.line(), base_location.line() + 3);
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)///
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)/// // Better: will report the location of `.context`.
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)/// # let base_location = location!();
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)/// # let error_future = async { AnotherSnafu.fail::<()>() };
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)/// let wrapped_error_future = async { error_future.await.context(ImplicitLocationSnafu) };
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)/// # let wrapped_error = wrapped_error_future.await.unwrap_err();
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)/// # assert_eq!(wrapped_error.location.line(), base_location.line() + 2);
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)///
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)/// // Better: Will report the location of `location!`
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)/// # let base_location = location!();
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)/// # let error_future = async { AnotherSnafu.fail::<()>() };
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)/// let wrapped_error_future = error_future.with_context(|_| ExplicitLocationSnafu {
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)///     location: location!(),
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)/// });
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)/// # let wrapped_error = wrapped_error_future.await.unwrap_err();
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)/// # assert_eq!(wrapped_error.location.line(), base_location.line() + 3);
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)///
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)/// # #[derive(Debug, Snafu)] struct AnotherError;
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)/// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)/// struct ImplicitLocationError {
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)///     source: AnotherError,
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)///     #[snafu(implicit)]
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)///     location: snafu::Location,
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)/// }
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)///
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)/// #[derive(Debug, Snafu)]
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)/// struct ExplicitLocationError {
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)///     source: AnotherError,
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)///     location: snafu::Location,
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)/// }
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)/// # };
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)/// # futures::executor::block_on(body);
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)/// # }
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)/// ```
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)pub type Location = &'static core::panic::Location<'static>;
